correctness.rationale: The universal covering strip is convex; every quotient geodesic has a straight shortest lift. The two nearest horizontal deck-image parities have displacements a and C-a. A measure-preserving reflection of a sampled transverse coordinate constructs the stated stochastic coupling. Uniform a and the exact diamond density of (Y1+Y2,Y2-Y1) yield the nonnegative one-dimensional integral. Its support and a positive-measure witness prove the strict region. Boundary-layer integration over a=C/2-t, 0<=t<=epsilon gives the epsilon^(3/2) coefficient 8/(3 H sqrt(C)) with O(epsilon^2) remainder. The common exact local CDF has coefficients pi/(CH) and -4/(3CH^2), which reconstruct positive C,H. Direct deck-image Monte Carlo and quadrature checks corroborate but are not substitutes for the analytic proof.

value.rationale: The two natural flat interval bundles have the same area, total boundary length, and every sufficiently small pair-distance probability, yet a global topological half-twist is detected by a sharp 3/2 onset and strict all-threshold stochastic gap thereafter. The exact positive coefficient gives a natural quantification of this global discrepancy, and the local coefficients plus global comparison reconstruct the geometry and orientability within the whole rectangular two-family class. This is a motivated inverse metric-probability theorem rather than a numerical table or an unmotivated special radius.
